# Synthetic budget workbook fixtures

Generated by `scripts/generate-budget-fixtures.mjs`. All figures are
fictional — see `docs/19_OPEN_DECISIONS.md` (D-005): no real 2026 workbook
was available in the build workspace, so these reproduce the documented
sheet structure (May/June/July/August + Core expenses) for ingestion
testing, not real financial data.

| File | Scenario |
|---|---|
| `2026-budget-v1-base.xlsx` | Baseline workbook: May, June, July, August, Core expenses |
| `2026-budget-v2-modified-august.xlsx` | August groceries figure corrected — MODIFIED sheet classification |
| `2026-budget-v3-renamed-august.xlsx` | August sheet renamed to "Aug-26" — DELETED_RENAMED classification |
| `2026-budget-v4-deleted-august.xlsx` | August sheet removed entirely — DELETED_RENAMED (deletion) classification |
| `2026-budget-v5-malformed.xlsx` | Text in a numeric cell, a blank row, a malformed date — validation/Needs Review path |
| `2026-budget-v6-unexpected-sheet.xlsx` | An extra sheet matching neither month nor reference conventions |
| `2026-budget-v7-identical-reupload.xlsx` | Content-identical to v1, freshly written — idempotent re-upload test |

Regenerate with:

```bash
node scripts/generate-budget-fixtures.mjs
```

**When the real 2026 workbook is supplied**, add it under a path excluded
from version control (e.g. `data/real-workbook/`, already gitignored) and
validate the M3 ingestion parser against it directly — these fixtures do not
replace that validation step.
